calls.reason: RoboPAIR and RoboHarm show LLM-controlled robots will carry out harmful actions, and RoboGuard shows safeguards cut that sharply. No source compares robots with home assistants, so the comparison can't be called.
This is a hedged opinion ('I don't think'). Amazon's 2022 blog speaks only to cloud capacity, and Fortune's data and GPU shortages date from after 2023, so the evidence doesn't settle the 2022 cause.

Code as Policies already turned commands into robot code, and SayCan reached 74% execution with clear failures left over. Neither isolates how reliably sentences map to actions, so the evidence is mixed.
Alexa+ now converses freely, but no study measures whether user expectations rose or went mostly unmet. One Consumer Reports reviewer was largely satisfied, which is too thin to call it either way.

Amazon says tens of millions joined Alexa+ Early Access within about three years, which strains 'long, long way away'. But that is the company's own claim, reliability at household scale is unmeasured, and Consumer Reports still found bugs.
